cues.text: Type One hypersensitivity is an immediate, allergic reaction.
It is provoked by re-exposure to a specific antigen, called an allergen.
CD4+ Th2 cells stimulate B cells to produce IgE antibodies specific to that antigen.
So the answer is immunoglobulin E.
Not IgA, IgD or IgG: for Type One, think IgE.
Examples include allergic asthma and anaphylaxis.
